questions.text: Only low relays (10 mm) fit the 503 box, and they give only basic electrical insulation between the 230 V contacts and the battery side. How should the battery stay safe to touch?
options: Low relays plus a screw-fixed battery cover, insulated probe tips, and an instruction to switch off the heating breaker before changing the battery (about +0.3 USD; good for the 10 prototypes, needs a safety review before CE)

Low relays plus an isolated relay driver, so the battery can be changed at any time (recommended for a home product: about +3 USD, parts about 20-23 USD, measurement every 15 min to keep the battery life, board space is tight)
Taller relays with reinforced insulation (about +2-5 USD, about 1 month less battery life, likely does not fit the 503 box)
questions.why: Safety requirement R8: a person who touches the battery or a probe must be protected by reinforced insulation. The low relay has 4 mm of internal creepage, and reinforced insulation needs 5 mm (conflicts.md C12).

questions.text: What do the outputs switch in practice?
options: Thermal valve heads, or zone valve motors drawing under 1.5 A per output (recommended: the low relay is rated for this)
Zone valve motors or pumps drawing more than 1.5 A per output (needs a bigger relay that does not fit the box)
questions.why: The low relay breaks 5 A of resistive load but only 1.5 A of motor (inductive) load at 230 V. Thermal heads use about 0.01-0.3 A each (conflicts.md C13).

questions.text: How often should the thermostat measure the rooms and switch the heating?
options: Every 10 minutes (recommended: about 14 months on an alkaline AA, 2.3 years on lithium)
Every 5 minutes (about 13.4 months alkaline, no safety margin on battery life)
Every 15 minutes (about 14.3 months alkaline, slower reaction)
questions.why: Each measurement wakes the Wi-Fi chip for about 0.1 s. Measuring every minute would cut the alkaline life to about 10 months. Thermal heads take 3-5 minutes to open, so 10 minutes changes the room temperature very little (conflicts.md C9).
